content.title: Vector Addition, Subtraction, and Scalar Multiplication
content.overview: This lesson covers the fundamental operations of combining vectors in a 2D plane. You will learn how to scale vectors by a constant and how to add or subtract them by manipulating their individual x and y components.
learning_objectives: Perform scalar multiplication on a vector by scaling each component.
Add and subtract vectors using component-wise operations.
Evaluate complex vector expressions involving both scalars and subtraction.
Verify vector calculations by tracking signs and re-checking individual components.

sections.title: Understanding Vector Components
sections.content: In the ACT, a 2D vector is typically represented as an ordered pair (x, y). The first number represents the horizontal component (x), and the second number represents the vertical component (y). Operations on vectors are performed 'component-wise,' meaning you handle the x-values and y-values separately.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication
sections.content: A scalar is a real number used to scale a vector. To multiply a vector by a scalar 'c', you multiply both the x and y components by that number: c(x, y) = (cx, cy). Geometrically, this stretches or shrinks the vector and may reverse its direction if the scalar is negative.

sections.title: Vector Addition and Subtraction
sections.content: To add two vectors, add their corresponding components: (u_x, u_y) + (v_x, v_y) = (u_x + v_x, u_y + v_y). To subtract vectors, subtract the components: (u_x, u_y) - (v_x, v_y) = (u_x - v_x, u_y - v_y). A helpful strategy for subtraction is to treat it as adding a negative scalar: u - v is the same as u + (-1)v.

sections.title: The Scale-Then-Combine Strategy
sections.content:
When faced with a complex expression like 2u - 3v, follow these steps: 1. Scale each vector by its respective scalar first. 2. Distribute any negative signs into the components immediately to avoid subtraction errors. 3. Sum the resulting x-components and y-components separately to find the final ordered pair.

![A flowchart showing the steps: Scale Vectors, Distribute Signs, Add Components, and Verify Result.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/36113b5c-0523-4d8c-b93d-770387a18c00-1786505554347-918.webp)

worked_examples.question: Given vectors u = (3, -2) and v = (-1, 4), calculate the resulting vector for the expression 2u - 3v.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Scale vector u by 2. 2 * (3, -2) = (6, -4). Step 2: Scale vector v by -3 (treating the subtraction as adding a negative). -3 * (-1, 4) = (3, -12). Step 3: Add the results component-wise. x-components: 6 + 3 = 9. y-components: -4 + (-12) = -16. The final vector is (9, -16).

common_mistakes: Forgetting to distribute the scalar to both components (only multiplying the x-value).
Sign errors during subtraction, especially when subtracting a negative component (e.g., thinking 6 - (-3) is 3 instead of 9).
Mixing up x and y components during the final addition step.
exam_tips: Always perform scalar multiplication before addition or subtraction.
If you are in a hurry, calculate just the x-component first; often, this will eliminate two or three incorrect multiple-choice options.
Double-check your signs! Negative scalars are the most common source of errors in vector problems.
content.recap: Vector operations are performed component-wise. Multiply every component by the scalar, then add or subtract the corresponding x and y values. Use the 'Scale-Then-Combine' method to maintain accuracy with signs.

knowledge_claims.content: A 2D vector is represented as an ordered pair (x, y) where x is the horizontal component and y is the vertical component.
To perform scalar multiplication, multiply both the x and y components of the vector by the scalar value.
The formula for scalar multiplication is c(x, y) = (cx, cy).
Vector addition is performed by adding the x-components together and the y-components together separately.
Vector subtraction u - v is mathematically equivalent to adding the vector u to the vector v scaled by -1.
When evaluating an expression like au + bv, scalar multiplication must be completed for both vectors before adding them together.
A common error is failing to distribute a negative scalar to the second (y) component of a vector.
To verify a vector result, re-calculate the x and y components independently to ensure no sign errors occurred during summation.
If a scalar is negative, the resulting vector will point in the opposite direction of the original vector.
In the expression 3(2, -1), the resulting vector is (6, -3).
The sum of vectors (5, 2) and (-1, 3) is (4, 5).
Unlike scalar addition, vector addition requires keeping horizontal and vertical movements distinct.
